We don't support the PPC architecture ourselves and most likely don't have the engineer bandwidth to maintain such a build.

But we wouldn't object if the community wanted to supported ppc64le. There are likely two pieces:
* making XLA work on PPC (probably mostly a matter of linking in the right LLVM backend in the TensorFlow/XLA tree)
* maintaining jaxlib builds.

Contributions welcome!
As to your specific question, I'd make sure that MKLDNN is disabled in the build (I believe there is an option to build.py for this.) I doubt MKLDNN works on non-Intel architectures.

Do you have the same problem if you try to build TensorFlow? We share a lot of build infrastructure with them, so I'm wondering if this is JAX specific or a more general Bazel/TF problem.

(Ultimately we don't have cycles to work on this, but we welcome contributions!)

@f0uriest If you can share the output of the build, we might be able to suggest things to change.

I'd speculate there are two or three things you'd need to do :
a) update `build.py` to pass the correct flags, if it isn't already doing so.
b) make sure XLA links in the Power LLVM backend if targeting Power. There are already cases for x86 and ARM; I don't recall if Power is included.
c) add a Power case to `build_wheel.py`.

HEY GUYS!  I got jax 0.4.25 to compile on ppc64le!

Here's what I did:

- Ubuntu 20.04 on p8.
- Install CUDA 11.8 using the runfile installer from here: https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-11-8-0-download-archive?target_os=Linux&target_arch=ppc64le&Distribution=RHEL&target_version=8&target_type=runfile_local
- Install python 3.10 from the deadsnakes ppa repository
- Create a python venv
- Clone the jax repo and check out the v0.4.25 tag
- Get the dist release of bazel 6.2.0 and bootstrap it
- Clone the bazel repo and check out the 6.1.2 tag
- Use the built bazel 6.2.0 to build the 6.1.2 distfile:
  - ../bazel-6.2.0-dist/output/bazel build //:bazel-distfile --tool_java_runtime_version=local_jdk
- Unzip the built distfile located in bazel-bin/bazel-distfile.zip
- Bootstrap build bazel 6.1.2 and put the result in your /usr/local/bin
- Clone my modified xla: https://github.com/bhuntsman/xla.git
  - The only change here is to "manually cherry-pick" commit 574a844a6172b73b03ad2d2cf89d73389fea4522, which adds ppc64le support to tsl and implib_so
- Clone my modified boringssl: https://github.com/bhuntsman/boringssl.git
  - The changes here are to revert all the commits that removed ppc64le support, and then to regenerate all the bazel build files.
- cd into your jax directory and build as follows:
  - TMP=/tmp python build/build.py --noenable_mkl_dnn --enable_cuda --build_gpu_plugin --gpu_plugin_cuda_version=11 --bazel_options=--override_repository=boringssl=/home/build/repos/boringssl --bazel_options=--override_repository=xla=/home/build/repos/xla
 
Now we have a few challenges to get this integrated.  Chiefest of which is convincing the boringssl project to bring back ppc64le support.  Originally I was looking at jax 0.4.25 as I thought perhaps it might support CUDA 11.1, but found that no it requires 11.8 as a minimum.
